text: This executive briefing took one request and thirty-nine minutes.
Nobody stepped in along the way.
It starts with a plain-English request to an AI agent in GitHub Copilot CLI.
Research World Bank data, analyze it in Excel, then build a seven-slide briefing in PowerPoint.
First, the agent does the research.
It finds the World Bank's official indicators, tests the data service, and pulls twenty-five years for twenty-five economies.
Then it checks for gaps.
Next, Excel MCP Server. The agent drives the real Excel app.
It loads the data with Power Query, builds a Data Model with DAX measures, and adds analysis sheets, charts, and a PivotTable.
A checks sheet tests the key numbers.
When a step fails, the agent reads the error and tries another way.
Before it designs a single slide, the agent reads its results back from the workbook.
Every number on a slide comes from Excel.
Now, PowerPoint MCP Server.
The agent designs one slide as a template, exports it as a picture, and looks at it, the way a designer would.
Then it builds the other slides, with native, editable charts, headlines that state the insight, sources, and speaker notes.
It ran into a chart bug and a PowerPoint crash, and recovered on its own.
The result is a seven-slide briefing.
China's income per person grew almost six times.
The gap between the richest and poorest economies halved.
And internet use went from seven percent to ninety.
One request. Six hundred and twelve tool calls. Two MCP servers, and one AI model.
We checked the headline numbers against the World Bank. You still review the result, but the heavy lifting is done.
